Diagnostic plots for drmTMB models

Source: R/plot.R
plot.drmTMB.Rd

Residuals against the fitted values, residuals against the dose, a normal QQ plot of the residuals, and normal QQ plots of the predicted random effects, drawn as ggplot2 graphs on one page. Unlike plot.drc of drc, it draws residual diagnostics, not the fitted dose-response curve; for the curve, use predict.drmTMB on a grid of doses (see the vignette).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'drmTMB'
plot(
  x,
  which = 1:3,
  type = c("quantile", "pearson", "response"),
  random = TRUE,
  logdose = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  draw = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a drmTMB object

which

the plots to draw: 1 residuals against fitted values, 2 residuals against dose, 3 normal QQ plot of the residuals, 4 normal QQ plots of the predicted random effects (models with random effects only)

type

residual type, see residuals.drmTMB: "quantile" (default), "pearson" or "response"

random

if TRUE, residuals and fitted values include the predicted random effects

logdose

logarithmic dose axis; by default for the models on the log-dose scale (loglogistic, weibull1, weibull2, lognormal, braincousens, cedergreen)

ncol

number of columns of the page

seed

seed for the randomised quantile residuals

draw

if FALSE, the graphs are returned without drawing them

...

not used

Value

a list of ggplot objects, invisibly, named fitted, dose, qq and ranef, for changing or drawing single graphs

Details

The default randomised quantile residuals are standard normal under the model for all families, so the QQ plot is compared with the identity line; for the discrete families they are drawn uniformly within the jump of the distribution function at each observation, and seed makes the plots reproducible. For type="response", the QQ plot line goes through the quartiles. A lowess smoother (red) shows trends of the residuals against the fitted values and the dose.

For the models on the log-dose scale, the dose axis is logarithmic; observations at dose zero are drawn left of the smallest positive dose, separated by a dashed line.

The QQ plots of the random effects (which=4) show the predicted random effects of each parameter and grouping factor. They are shrunk towards zero, so their spread is smaller than the estimated standard deviation, and with few groups they say little about the normality of the random effects.

See also

residuals.drmTMB, predict.drmTMB

Examples

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
plot(mod)

# residuals against the dose only, on the log scale
plot(mod, which = 2, logdose = TRUE)
